key_insight: The paper introduces adaptive forward-gradient estimators for parameterised quantum circuits that reduce measurement cost while remaining unbiased, and generalise several known gradient methods as special cases.
engineering_relevance: This can substantially cut shot budgets and training time for large-scale PQC optimisation on near-term quantum hardware, improving practicality for quantum machine learning and variational algorithms.
method: Average random directional derivatives to form an unbiased forward-gradient estimate.
Use an adaptive allocation rule in QUIVER to minimise measurement cost per update.
Recover SPSA, random coordinate descent, and parameter-shift in limiting regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results on ECG5000 and MNIST with up to 60 qubits and 1770 parameters, plus benchmarks on QAOA and VQE where QUIVER outperforms iCANS and gCANS.
watch_item: Performance depends on choosing a suitable number of random directions and may still be limited by variance or hardware noise in real devices.
paper_title: Adaptive directional gradients for parameterised quantum circuits
